newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-PROST MAKES FRESH START AS TEAM BOSS.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-PROST MAKES FRESH START AS TEAM BOSS.

text.p: Four times world champion Alain Prost joined the ranks of Formula One team owners on Friday with the official launch of Prost Grand Prix.
"We will do the maximum to win races and to be competitive from 1997," the Frenchman promised.
Prost has taken over Ligier and will campaign their Mugen-Honda powered JS 45 cars in the world championship, starting with the season-opening Australian Grand Prix on March 9.
Olivier Panis of France and Shinji Nakano of Japan continue as drivers.
Prost's cars will be fitted with Peugeot V10 engines, currently used by the Jordan team, from 1998 to 2000.
"In 1997, it will be Prost-Mugen-Honda and in 1998 it will be Prost-Peugeot," said Prost, the most successful driver in grand prix racing.
When he quit the cockpit in 1993 the man dubbed 'the professor' because of his calculated and thoughtful approach to driving, had a record 51 victories behind him.

Prost, who worked as a television commentator and a technical advisor at McLaren after his retirement, needed the agreement of all the teams to change the Ligier name. But he had to wait until Tuesday to gain Jordan boss Eddie Jordan's signature.
Jordan was afraid he might lose his supply of Peugeot engines but was reassured when he learned that the deal reached by Prost would allow him to continue with the French company this year.
Peugeot president Jacques Calvet said the contract with Prost would allow Peugeot to supply engines to Jordan as well after 1997.
"I'm not saying we will but the contract we've signed with Alain Prost would make it possible," Calvet said.
Prost bought Ligier from Benetton boss Flavio Briatore of Italy, who had owned the team since 1994.

"I'm not telling you how much it was," said Prost, who spent some of his own money in the deal and is now the team's sole owner. "Anyway, it's always too expensive for the one who buys and too cheap for the one who sells."
Prost said his team's annual budget fron 1998 would be around 300 million francs ($53 million).
"It will be less than four other teams but it should allow us to be competitive," he said.

Ligier were created in 1976 and scored eight grand prix wins from 1977 to 1981. In 1994, the struggling outfit was bought by Briatore who wanted to obtain their Renault engine for his own Benetton cars.

Despite losing the Renault engine, Ligier improved under Briatore's rule and last year Panis scored a stunning victory in Monaco. They finished sixth in the constructors' world championship with 15 points.
"The team has improved a lot over the last few years and this year's car looks even more competitive," said Prost.
"That progress has been made with a team and it would be foolish not to keep that team," he added.
Prost said he had contacts with drivers, engineers and sponsors for 1998 but declined to name them.

"The idea was to create a French team," he said. "It's the case as Ligier are based in France and we will have a French engine and at least one French driver in 1998. But to have a 100 percent French team is impossible."
